panels.title: The Marriage of Draupadi — One Bow, One Fish, Five Brothers
panels.label: The Marriage of Draupadi
panels.summary: Draupadī is born full-grown from King Drupada's vengeance-sacrifice, and is won at her svayaṃvara by a disguised Arjuna, who pierces a spinning fish by its reflection alone. Kuntī's unretractable word then makes her the common wife of all five Pāṇḍavas.
panels.alt: King Drupada feeds the night fire in a pillared courtyard, asking the sacrifice for a weapon.
panels.caption: The sacrifice at Kāmpilya

panels.title: Samudra Manthan — The Churning of the Ocean
panels.label: Samudra Manthan
panels.summary: Devas and asuras churn the ocean of milk together to draw out amṛta, using Mount Mandara as the rod and the serpent Vāsuki as the rope, with Viṣṇu as the tortoise Kūrma beneath it. Fourteen treasures rise before the nectar, among them the Hālāhala poison that Śiva holds in his throat.
panels.alt: Vāsuki is wound taut as the churning-rope while Viṣṇu holds the coils.
panels.caption: The churning

panels.title: Vamana & Bali — Three Steps That Measured the Universe
panels.label: Vamana & Bali
panels.summary: Viṣṇu, born as a brahmin dwarf, asks the world-conquering asura king Bali for three paces of land, then swells into the cosmic Trivikrama and measures the universe in two strides. Bali keeps his word and offers his own head for the third.
panels.alt: Asura warriors stand over their fallen king Bali on a battlefield shore after the war for the nectar.

panels.title: Varaha & the Drowning Earth
panels.label: Varaha & the Drowning Earth
panels.summary: When Hiraṇyākṣa drags the Earth down into the lightless deep, Viṣṇu takes the form of a boar, dives after her and raises her on one tusk. The episode fuses an older cosmogonic boar who lifts the Earth at a kalpa's dawn with the killing of the first of Viṣṇu's cursed gatekeepers.
panels.alt: Brahmā looks out across a shoreless ocean at the dawn of a new creation, with no earth left to stand on.

panels.title: Prahlada & Narasimha — Neither Man Nor Beast, Neither Day Nor Night
panels.label: Prahlada & Narasimha
panels.summary: Hiraṇyakaśipu's boon leaves a gap in every direction — no man and no beast, neither day nor night, neither inside nor out — and his son Prahlāda's devotion to Viṣṇu is what finds it. Narasiṃha bursts from a pillar at dusk and satisfies every clause at once.
panels.alt: Hiraṇyakaśipu stands motionless in penance on Mount Mandara until an anthill closes over him.

panels.title: The Seventh Gate — Every Demon You Watched Fall Was the Same Two Souls
panels.label: The Seventh Gate
panels.summary: Viṣṇu's gatekeepers Jaya and Vijaya turn the four Kumāras away at the seventh gate of Vaikuṇṭha and are cursed to be born on earth. Given the choice, they take three lives as his enemies rather than seven as his devotees.
panels.alt: Jaya and Vijaya stand armed at the seventh gate of Vaikuṇṭha, the palace of light behind them.

panels.title: Matsya and the Deluge — One Small Mercy Saved the Whole World
panels.label: Matsya and the Deluge
panels.summary: A great horned fish warns the righteous king Satyavrata that a pralaya flood will drown the three worlds, and tells him to build a boat and load it with the seven sages and the seeds of all life. The boat rides out the deluge tethered to the fish's horn.
panels.alt: King Satyavrata stands in the river Kṛtamālā at dawn with a tiny fish lying in his cupped hands.

panels.title: Garuda and the Stolen Nectar — The Eagle Who Stormed Heaven to Free His Mother
panels.label: Garuda and the Stolen Nectar
panels.summary: Garuḍa's mother Vinatā is enslaved by her sister through a rigged wager, and the price named for her freedom is the amṛta the gods keep in heaven. He fights his way to it, wins deathlessness without drinking it, and frees her without breaking a promise.
panels.alt: Garuḍa rises fully formed from the second egg, blazing so bright that the gods mistake him for Agni.

panels.title: Mohini and Bhasmasura — The Boon That Turned on the Hand That Begged for It
panels.label: Mohini and Bhasmasura
panels.summary: Bhasmāsura wins a boon from Śiva that burns to ash whatever head his hand touches, then turns it on Śiva himself. Viṣṇu takes the form of Mohinī and leads the demon into a dance that ends with his own hand on his own head.
panels.alt: The boon settles as a flame into Bhasmāsura's cupped hands.

panels.title: Kaliya Daman — The Boy Who Danced on the Serpent King
panels.label: Kaliya Daman
panels.summary: The boy Kṛṣṇa leaps into a bend of the Yamunā poisoned by the many-hooded serpent Kāliya and dances on his hoods until he yields. The river runs clean again, and Kāliya is spared and sent away.
panels.alt: The poisoned bend of the Yamunā lies black and still, its trees scorched, one flowering kadamba left alive above it.

panels.title: Durga and Mahishasura — The Demon No God Could Kill
panels.label: Durga and Mahishasura
panels.summary: Mahiṣāsura's boon makes him proof against every god and every man, so the gods pour their combined fury into a single form and Durgā steps out of it. She meets him through every shape he takes and ends him with her triśūla and sword.
panels.alt: Streams of light pour from the face of every god and climb into a single mountain-tall column of fire.

panels.title: Sati and Daksha's Yajna — The Origin of the 51 Shakti Peethas
panels.label: Sati and Daksha's Yajna
panels.summary: Dakṣa holds a great sacrifice and allows Śiva no share in it, and his daughter Satī gives up by her own yogic fire the body her father gave her. Śiva's grief takes shape as Vīrabhadra, and the places where her body falls become the śakti pīṭhas.
panels.alt: Dakṣa's great sacrifice burns before an assembly of every god and sage — with no share set aside for Śiva.

panels.title: The Birth of Kartikeya — The Six-Faced God Who Slew Tarakasura
panels.label: The Birth of Kartikeya
panels.summary: Tārakāsura's boon allows only a son of Śiva to kill him, and Śiva is a widower sunk in meditation. The union of Śiva and Pārvatī produces a six-faced child who leads heaven's army at seven days old.
panels.alt: Brahmā comes down on his lotus to answer the penance that has scorched the three worlds.

panels.title: Gajendra Moksha — The Elephant King Saved by One Cry to Vishnu
panels.label: Gajendra Moksha
panels.summary: The elephant-king Gajendra is seized by a crocodile and fights for a thousand years without winning free. He is saved only when he stops fighting, lifts a single lotus, and calls on no god by name.
panels.alt: The three peaks of Trikūṭa rise from the Ocean of Milk above Ṛtumat's lake of lotuses.

panels.title: The Birth of Ganesha — How Ganesha Got His Elephant Head
panels.label: The Birth of Ganesha
panels.summary: Pārvatī shapes a son from her own body to guard her door, and Śiva, refused entry to his own house, strikes off the boy's head. He is restored with the head of an elephant and given the first worship at the start of every undertaking.
panels.alt: Pārvatī's son, shaped from her own body, takes up a staff at her word.

panels.title: Markandeya and Yama — The Boy Who Defeated Death
panels.label: Markandeya and Yama
panels.summary: Mārkaṇḍeya is given a brilliant life of only sixteen years, and on the last day he holds on to a śivaliṅga. Śiva comes out of the stone as Kālāntaka, strikes Death down, and leaves the boy sixteen forever.
panels.alt: Mārkaṇḍeya wraps both arms around the śivaliṅga on the last day of his sixteenth year.

panels.title: Parashurama — The Sage Who Beheaded His Own Mother — Sixth Avatar of Vishnu
panels.label: Parashurama
panels.summary: Paraśurāma obeys his father's order to kill his own mother, then spends his one reward on asking for her life back. When Kārtavīrya's sons kill his father, he sweeps the earth of kṣatriya kings twenty-one times over.
panels.alt: The Bhṛgu hermitage deep in the forest, where Jamadagni, Reṇukā and the cow Kāmadhenu live.

panels.title: Karna's Golden Armor
panels.label: Karna's Golden Armor
panels.summary: Karṇa is born wearing golden armour and earrings fused to his skin, and while they stay on him he cannot be killed. Indra comes as a beggar at the one hour Karṇa's vow cannot refuse, and Karṇa cuts them from his own body.
panels.alt: Kuntī sets the basket holding her armoured child upon the river, her hand holding on a moment longer.

panels.title: Krishna and Sudama — The Fistful of Rice That Became a Palace
panels.label: Krishna and Sudama
panels.summary: Sudāmā, a poor brahmin and Kṛṣṇa's boyhood schoolmate, walks to Dvārakā with a handful of borrowed flattened rice and cannot bring himself to ask for anything. Kṛṣṇa washes his feet, eats the rice, and sends him home to a house he never requested.
panels.alt: Sudāmā's wife knots a small handful of borrowed flattened rice into a scrap of torn cloth.

panels.title: Krishna Lifts Govardhan — Seven Days Under a Mountain
panels.label: Krishna Lifts Govardhan
panels.summary: Kṛṣṇa persuades the cowherds of Vraja to honour the hill Govardhana rather than Indra, and Indra answers with seven days of storm. Kṛṣṇa lifts the whole hill on one finger and holds it up until the clouds wear themselves out.
panels.alt: Kṛṣṇa among the cowherds of Vraja, before the hill they will honour.
panels.caption: The first annakūṭa

panels.title: Bhagiratha and the Descent of Ganga — The River Shiva Caught in His Hair
panels.label: Bhagiratha and the Descent of…
panels.summary: Sixty thousand sons of King Sagara are burnt to ash by the sage Kapila's glance, and only the river of heaven can release them. Bhagīratha's penance brings Gaṅgā down, and Śiva catches her fall in his hair.
panels.alt: Sagara's sons find their horse beside the sage Kapila, deep in pātāla.

panels.title: Kali and Raktabija — The Demon Who Multiplied From His Own Blood
panels.hi: काली और रक्तबीज: अपने ही रक्त से बढ़ता असुर
panels.label: Kali and Raktabija
panels.summary: Raktabīja's boon makes every drop of his spilled blood stand up as another Raktabīja, so wounding him only multiplies him. Kālī, sprung from Durgā's brow, drinks each drop before it can reach the ground.
panels.alt: Kālī springs fully formed from the knot of Durgā's frowning brow, black-skinned, garlanded with skulls.

panels.title: Tripurantaka — The Three Flying Cities
panels.label: Tripurantaka
panels.summary: Three asura brothers win three flying cities that can be destroyed only by a single arrow, at the one instant in a thousand years when the cities align. Śiva waits for that instant on a chariot built from the earth, the sun and the moon.
panels.alt: The first of the three flying cities, built of gold, riding in the heavens.

panels.title: Krishna and Kamsa — The King Who Feared a Boy Before He Was Born
panels.hi: कृष्ण और कंस — वह राजा जो जन्म से पहले ही एक बालक से डरता था
panels.label: Krishna and Kamsa
panels.summary: Kaṃsa hears a voice promise that his sister's eighth child will kill him, and spends his life trying to prevent it. Kṛṣṇa comes to Mathurā for a bow-sacrifice that is really a trap, and takes the king down from his own high seat.
panels.alt: Dawn over the river, the black fort of Mathurā standing on the far bank.

panels.title: Narakasura and Satyabhama — The Queen Who Took the Reins
panels.hi: नरकासुर और सत्यभामा: जब रानी ने लगाम थामी
panels.label: Narakasura and Satyabhama
panels.summary: Narakāsura's boon leaves one clause open — only his own mother can end him — and his mother is the earth, Bhūdevī, incarnate as Kṛṣṇa's queen Satyabhāmā. The campaign frees sixteen thousand captive women, and the day before Dīvālī still carries the demon's name.
panels.alt: Kṛṣṇa and Satyabhāmā climb away from the white sea-city of Dvārakā on Garuḍa at first light.

panels.title: Krishna and the Syamantaka Jewel — The Sun-Gem That Made Him a Suspect
panels.hi: कृष्ण और स्यमन्तक मणि — वह सूर्य-मणि जिसने उन्हें आरोपी बना दिया
panels.label: Krishna and the Syamantaka…
panels.summary: The Syamantaka gem yields gold every day and destroys a wearer who does not deserve it. When its owner's brother is killed on a hunt, Dvārakā suspects Kṛṣṇa, and he has to track the jewel into a bear king's cave to clear his own name.
panels.alt: Sūrya gives Satrājit the Syamantaka, the gem that makes eight bhāra of gold a day.

panels.title: Lingodbhava — The Pillar of Fire No God Could Measure
panels.hi: लिंगोद्भव — वह अग्नि-स्तंभ जिसका छोर किसी देवता को न मिला
panels.label: Lingodbhava
panels.summary: Brahmā and Viṣṇu argue over which of them is the first cause, and a pillar of fire rises between them with no top and no base. Viṣṇu admits he found no end; Brahmā claims a summit he never reached, and Śiva steps out of the pillar having heard both.
panels.alt: Brahmā and Viṣṇu stand face to face, each claiming to be the first cause of everything.

panels.title: Kama's Ashes, Parvati's Vow — Kamadeva Dahan
panels.hi: कामदेव का दहन और पार्वती का तप
panels.label: Kama's Ashes, Parvati's Vow
panels.summary: The gods send Kāmadeva to break Śiva's meditation so that a son can be born who will kill Tārakāsura, and Śiva's third eye burns him to ash. Pārvatī then wins Śiva by her own austerity rather than by an arrow.
panels.alt: Tārakāsura sits on the throne of heaven, which his boon has made it impossible for any god to take back.

panels.title: Arjuna and the Hunter of Indrakila — Kiratarjuniya, Shiva's Test
panels.label: Arjuna and the Hunter of…
panels.summary: During the Pāṇḍavas' forest exile, Arjuna goes north alone to win the weapons the coming war will need. Śiva meets him as a mountain hunter, beats him in a quarrel over a boar, and gives him the Pāśupata.
panels.alt: Indrakīla at first light: a vast grey-blue Himalayan massif above the treeline.

panels.title: Barbarik — Three Arrows Were Enough
panels.label: Barbarik
panels.summary: Barbarīka comes to Kurukṣetra with three infallible arrows and a promise to his mother to fight for whichever side is losing — which would make the war unwinnable by either. Kṛṣṇa asks him for his head, and gives it a hilltop from which to watch the whole war.
panels.alt: A single arrow rises into the pīpal canopy and pierces leaf after leaf.

panels.title: Dhruva — The Five-Year-Old Who Became the Pole Star
panels.hi: ध्रुव: पाँच बरस का वह बालक जो ध्रुवतारा बन गया
panels.label: Dhruva
panels.summary: Refused a place on his father's lap at five years old, Dhruva walks into the forest alone to find Viṣṇu himself. He is granted the kingdom he no longer wants, and the one fixed point at the top of the sky.
panels.alt: Five-year-old Dhruva reaches toward his father's lap, his hand still raised when he is stopped.

panels.title: Savitri and Satyavan — She Followed Death Down the Road
panels.hi: सावित्री और सत्यवान: वह मृत्यु के पीछे-पीछे चल पड़ी
panels.label: Savitri and Satyavan
panels.summary: Sāvitrī marries Satyavān knowing he has a year to live, and when Yama comes for him she follows Death down the southern road. She argues four boons out of him before asking for the one that returns her husband.
panels.alt: One forest clearing holds the whole final year at once — spring blossom, summer dust, monsoon rain, autumn leaves, winter mist.

panels.title: Ekalavya and the Teacher Made of Clay
panels.label: Ekalavya and the Teacher Made…
panels.summary: Refused instruction by Droṇa, the forest prince Ekalavya makes a clay image of the teacher and trains before it until he outshoots the Kuru princes. Droṇa then claims the one fee that disarms him: his right thumb.
panels.alt: Young Ekalavya presses the last of the wet clay onto the teacher he has made for himself.

panels.title: Abhimanyu and the Chakravyuha — Not Out
panels.label: Abhimanyu and the Chakravyuha
panels.summary: Abhimanyu knows how to break into Droṇa's cakravyūha but not how to get out of it, and goes in anyway when no one else can. The formation closes behind him and he fights on alone until only a broken chariot wheel is left him.
panels.alt: Droṇa's Cakravyūha seen whole from above, built entirely of soldiers, chariots and standards.

panels.title: Why Brahma Has Almost No Temples — The Fifth Head Shiva Cut Off
panels.hi: ब्रह्मा के मंदिर क्यों नहीं हैं — ब्रह्मा का पाँचवाँ सिर
panels.label: Why Brahma Has Almost No…
panels.summary: Brahmā raises a fifth head and makes a claim that Śiva hears out in silence; Bhairava takes the head off with a single stroke. The skull clings to Bhairava's hand until it falls at a place of release — and Brahmā is left with almost no temples of his own.
panels.alt: Brahmā raises a fifth face above the four, and the gathered devas look up uneasily.

panels.title: Vrinda and Jalandhara — Why a Tulsi Plant Is Married to a Stone
panels.hi: वृंदा और जलंधर — तुलसी हर वर्ष एक पत्थर से क्यों ब्याही जाती है
panels.label: Vrinda and Jalandhara
panels.summary: Jālandhara cannot be killed while his wife Vṛndā's chastity is intact, so the gods win by māyā rather than by weapons. Vṛndā walks into the fire, and a tulsī plant grows from her ashes — married each year to a śālagrāma stone.
panels.alt: In a household courtyard at dusk, a woman garlands a tulsī plant beside a small black śālagrāma stone.

panels.title: Yayati — The King Who Borrowed His Son's Youth
panels.hi: यायाति: वह राजा जिसने पुत्र से यौवन उधार लिया
panels.label: Yayati
panels.summary: Cursed with premature old age, King Yayāti asks his sons to trade their youth for it, and only the youngest, Puru, agrees. A thousand years of indulgence teach him that desire is never ended by feeding it.
panels.alt: An unnaturally aged Yayāti reaches toward his youngest son Puru, who stands young and straight before him.

panels.title: Shakuntala — The Ring Was Never in the Original
panels.label: Shakuntala
panels.summary: Duṣyanta marries Śakuntalā at her forest hermitage and then refuses to know her when she comes to his court with their son. The epic's own telling has no curse and no ring: a voice from the sky settles it, and the boy becomes Bharata.
panels.alt: King Duṣyanta walks alone into Kaṇva's forest hermitage.

panels.title: Ashwatthama — The Sentence Krishna Chose Instead of Death
panels.hi: अश्वत्थामा: कृष्ण ने मृत्यु के बदले जो दंड चुना
panels.label: Ashwatthama
panels.summary: After the war is already decided, Aśvatthāman kills the Pāṇḍava camp in its sleep and then looses a weapon at an unborn child. Kṛṣṇa takes the gem from his forehead and gives him a sentence to live out rather than a death.
panels.alt: A grounded pre-war portrait of Aśvatthāman, the small dark-blue gem in his forehead clearly visible.

panels.title: Surya's Shadow Wife — Sanjna, Chhaya and the Birth of Shani
panels.hi: सूर्य की छाया-पत्नी: संज्ञा, छाया और शनि का जन्म
panels.label: Surya's Shadow Wife
panels.summary: Saṃjñā cannot bear her husband Sūrya's light and leaves her own shadow, Chāyā, in her place, and the substitution holds for years. Chāyā's son is Śani, and his father's doubt about him is where the planet's reputation begins.
panels.alt: In a shaded palace courtyard Saṃjñā faces Chāyā, the shadow double she is leaving in her place.

panels.title: The Cloth Would Not End — Draupadi in the Dice Hall
panels.hi: वस्त्र बढ़ता गया, सभा देखती रही — द्रौपदी चीरहरण
panels.label: The Cloth Would Not End
panels.summary: Yudhiṣṭhira stakes and loses his kingdom, his brothers, himself and finally Draupadī at a rigged game of dice. Draupadī's question to the assembly — whether a man who has already lost himself can stake another — is the one no one in the hall can answer.
panels.alt: The dice hall at Hastināpura, where dice kept falling and kingdoms kept changing hands.

panels.title: Arjuna Refused to Fight — Then Krishna Showed Him Time
panels.hi: अर्जुन ने युद्ध से मना किया—फिर कृष्ण ने काल दिखाया
panels.label: Arjuna Refused to Fight
panels.summary: Arjuna sets down his bow between the two armies rather than fight his own kin, and Kṛṣṇa answers him. Chapters seven to twelve turn the teaching toward devotion and open into the Viśvarūpa, the form in which Arjuna sees time itself.
panels.alt: Before the first arrow flies at Kurukṣetra, the blind king Dhṛtarāṣṭra asks what the two sides have done.

panels.title: Why Vaishno Devi Granted Bhairavnath Liberation
panels.hi: वैष्णो देवी ने भैरवनाथ को वरदान क्यों दिया?
panels.label: Why Vaishno Devi Granted…
panels.summary: Pursued by the tantric Bhairavnāth, the goddess takes refuge in a cave on Trikūṭa for nine months. At the cave she ends him — and then grants him liberation and a shrine of his own above hers.
panels.alt: High on Trikūṭa, pilgrims enter the holy cave and bow before three sacred stone piṇḍīs.

panels.title: Ganesha Never Left Home — and Won the World
panels.hi: गणेश घर से निकले ही नहीं—फिर भी संसार जीत लिया
panels.label: Ganesha Never Left Home
panels.summary: Nārada brings a single fruit to Kailāsa, and Śiva and Pārvatī set their two sons a race around the world for it. Kārttikeya circles the three worlds; Gaṇeśa walks around his parents and wins — and the victory costs the family Kārttikeya, who leaves Kailāsa for Palani.
panels.alt: Kārttikeya returns to Kailāsa with the wind of three worlds still streaming from his peacock's feathers.

panels.title: Karna Used the One Weapon Meant for Arjuna
panels.hi: कर्ण ने अर्जुन के लिए बचा अस्त्र किस पर चलाया?
panels.label: Karna Used the One Weapon…
panels.summary: On the fourteenth night of the war, Ghaṭotkaca's rākṣasa power is destroying the Kaurava army in the dark. Karṇa spends the Vāsavī Śakti — the one weapon he had kept back for Arjuna — to stop him, and while the Pāṇḍavas grieve, Kṛṣṇa rejoices.
panels.alt: A single golden dart crosses the torch-lit darkness while a colossal warrior fills the moonlit sky before it.

panels.title: When Karna’s Wheel Sank — The Final Battle
panels.hi: जब कर्ण का पहिया धँसा — अंतिम युद्ध
panels.label: When Karna’s Wheel Sank
panels.summary: Two curses fall due on the seventeenth day: Karṇa's weapons desert his memory and his chariot wheel sinks into the earth. He asks for time under the rules of war, and Kṛṣṇa reminds him of the rules his own side had already broken.
panels.alt: On the seventeenth day of Kurukṣetra, two chariots move toward the duel the war had delayed for a lifetime.

panels.title: Krishna Took the Bride — Because She Asked Him To
panels.hi: कृष्ण दुल्हन को ले गए—क्योंकि उसी ने बुलाया था
panels.label: Krishna Took the Bride
panels.summary: Rukmiṇī sends Kṛṣṇa a letter asking him to come before her brother can marry her to someone else, and sets out the plan herself. What follows is a rescue she solicited, not a raid for plunder.
panels.alt: Before dawn in Kuṇḍina, Rukmiṇī presses a sealed letter into a trusted brahmin's hands.

panels.title: She Came to Kill Baby Krishna — He Gave Her Liberation
panels.hi: मारने आई पूतना को कृष्ण ने मोक्ष क्यों दिया?
panels.label: She Came to Kill Baby Krishna
panels.summary: Pūtanā comes to Gokula disguised as a beautiful nurse, with poison on her breast, to kill the infant Kṛṣṇa. He takes her life along with her milk, and gives her the liberation owed to a mother.
panels.alt: Before Gokula fully wakes, a beautiful stranger crosses Nanda's threshold carrying poison on her body.

panels.title: They Opened the Door Too Soon — and Found Jagannath
panels.hi: दरवाज़ा जल्दी खुला—और जगन्नाथ का रूप मिला
panels.label: They Opened the Door Too Soon
panels.summary: Vidyāpati traces the hidden forest worship of Nīla Mādhava, and King Indradyumna is told to carve an image from a log that comes to the Odisha shore. The old craftsman who takes the work asks only to be left undisturbed until it is done; the door is opened too soon, and the unfinished forms are installed exactly as they are.
panels.alt: Every summer three immense chariots roll through Puri as countless hands pull the Lord of the Universe into the street.

panels.title: The Palace Was Built to Burn the Pandavas Alive
panels.hi: पांडवों को जलाने के लिए बनाया गया था यह महल
panels.label: The Palace Was Built to Burn…
panels.summary: Duryodhana has a palace of lac built at Vāraṇāvata so that the Pāṇḍavas will burn inside it, and Vidura warns Yudhiṣṭhira in code. They escape through a tunnel, and the Niṣāda woman and her five sons who die in the fire let the world believe the Pāṇḍavas burned with it.
panels.alt: Above the concealed passage, a palace blazes so fiercely that its lacquered walls seem to melt into the night.

panels.title: Draupadī
panels.label: Draupadī
panels.summary: The epic offers multiple, mutually incompatible explanations for her polyandry — preserve all. - Variant A — Incarnation of Śrī/Lakṣmī (Ādi Parva 1.196) [Critical Edition]: Indra speaks insolently to Śiva at dice and is cursed; five proud "Indras" are sent to earth as the…
panels.alt: The arena at Kāmpilya — the fish-target on its wheel above the black pool of oil.
panels.artFilmTitle: The Marriage of Draupadi — One Bow, One Fish, Five Brothers

panels.title: Drupada — the Pāñcāla King Whose Vengeance Lit the War-Altar
panels.label: Drupada
panels.alt: King Drupada feeds the night fire in a pillared courtyard, asking the sacrifice for a weapon.
panels.artFilmTitle: The Marriage of Draupadi — One Bow, One Fish, Five Brothers

panels.title: Ādi Parva — The Book of the Beginning
panels.label: Ādi Parva
panels.summary: The Ādi Parva ("Book of the Beginning") is the first of the eighteen parvas of the Mahābhārata — the longest single book, divided traditionally into 19 upaparvas (sub-parvas), spanning ~236 adhyāyas in the Calcutta/Bombay vulgate. It establishes the frame narration, the cosmic…
panels.alt: Draupadī places the marigold garland around the young brahmin's neck as the arena looks on.
panels.artFilmTitle: The Marriage of Draupadi — One Bow, One Fish, Five Brothers

panels.title: Samudra Manthana — The Churning of the Ocean
panels.label: Samudra Manthana
panels.summary: The Samudra Manthana ("churning of the ocean") — also Kshira-Sagara Manthana (churning of the milk-ocean), Amrita Manthana — is one of the most widely depicted episodes in Hindu tradition. The Devas and Asuras jointly churn the cosmic ocean to extract amrita, using Mount Mandara…
panels.alt: Lakṣmī rises from the sea on a lotus, attended by elephants.
panels.artFilmTitle: Samudra Manthan — The Churning of the Ocean

panels.title: Vāmana, Bali & Trivikrama — the Three Strides
panels.label: Vāmana, Bali & Trivikrama
panels.summary: The Vāmana–Bali episode tells how Viṣṇu, born as a tiny brahmin dwarf, begs three paces of land from the world-conquering Asura king Bali, then swells into the cosmic Trivikrama ("three-strides") form to measure the whole universe in two steps — reclaiming the three worlds for…
panels.alt: A banana-leaf feast laid for Onam in a Kerala doorway, the room flooded with light.
panels.artFilmTitle: Vamana & Bali — Three Steps That Measured the Universe

panels.title: Varāha — the Boar Avatar and the Slaying of Hiraṇyākṣa
panels.label: Varāha
panels.summary: The Varāha descent is told most fully in the Bhāgavata Purāṇa, Skandha 3 — the cosmogony of Maitreya to Vidura, with the boar's emergence at SB 3.13 and the war with Hiraṇyākṣa at SB 3.17–19 — and in compact form in Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.4 and across the Varāha Purāṇa. It is unusual…
panels.alt: Varāha carries Bhū-devī onto the restored Earth as light breaks over the calmed water.
panels.artFilmTitle: Varaha & the Drowning Earth

panels.title: Prahlāda & Narasiṃha — the Man-Lion's Descent
panels.label: Prahlāda & Narasiṃha
panels.summary: The Prahlāda–Narasiṃha cycle is told in the Bhāgavata Purāṇa, Skandha 7, chapters 1–10 (SB 7.1–7.10), narrated by Nārada to Yudhiṣṭhira. It is the longest sustained avatāra-narrative in the Purāṇa's early skandhas and the doctrinal home of dveṣa-bhakti (liberation through total…
panels.alt: Hiraṇyakaśipu stands motionless in penance on Mount Mandara until an anthill closes over him.
panels.artFilmTitle: Prahlada & Narasimha — Neither Man Nor Beast, Neither Day Nor Night

panels.title: Jaya & Vijaya — the Three-Birth Curse
panels.label: Jaya & Vijaya

panels.alt: Jaya and Vijaya fall from Vaikuṇṭha, their haloes guttering as horns break from their brows.

panels.title: Daśāvatāra — The Ten Avatars of Vishnu
panels.label: Daśāvatāra
panels.summary: In order as enumerated in Bhagavata Canto 1 Ch. 3: (1) the Four Kumaras, (2) Varaha, (3) Narada, (4) Nara-Narayana, (5) Kapila, (6) Dattatreya, (7) Yajña, (8) Rishabha, (9) Prithu, (10) Matsya, (11) Kurma, (12) Dhanvantari, (13) Mohini, (14) Narasimha, (15) Vamana, (16)…
panels.alt: Jaya and Vijaya stand armed at the seventh gate of Vaikuṇṭha, the palace of light behind them.
panels.artFilmTitle: The Seventh Gate — Every Demon You Watched Fall Was the Same Two Souls

panels.title: Matsya avatāra (the Fish and the Pralaya-Flood)
panels.label: Matsya avatāra
panels.summary: The Matsya ("fish") avatāra tells how Viṣṇu, as a great horned fish, warns the righteous Manu — Vaivasvata in the Purāṇas, Satyavrata before his Manu-hood — of a world-ending pralaya flood, instructs him to build a boat, load it with the seeds of all life and the seven sages…
panels.alt: The boat rides the flood, bound by the serpent Vāsuki to Matsya's golden horn.
panels.artFilmTitle: Matsya and the Deluge — One Small Mercy Saved the Whole World

panels.title: Garuḍa — King of Birds, Mount of Viṣṇu
panels.label: Garuḍa
panels.alt: Indra's vajra strikes Garuḍa in flight and cannot harm him at all.
panels.artFilmTitle: Garuda and the Stolen Nectar — The Eagle Who Stormed Heaven to Free His Mother

panels.title: Mohini: Vishnu's Enchantress Form
panels.label: Mohini: Vishnu's Enchantress…
panels.alt: The hand that hunted Śiva, burning — the gift spent on the one who begged for it.
panels.artFilmTitle: Mohini and Bhasmasura — The Boon That Turned on the Hand That Begged for It

panels.title: Bhasmāsura & Vṛkāsura — Shiva's Dangerous Boons
panels.label: Bhasmāsura & Vṛkāsura
panels.summary: These are two retellings of one narrative kernel — a devotee-asura wins from Śiva the power to reduce to ashes (bhasma) whomever he touches on the head, then tries it on Śiva himself; Viṣṇu intervenes by guile and the asura's own hand lands on his own head. The textually…
panels.alt: Only bright ash drifts down in the glade where the demon had danced.
panels.artFilmTitle: Mohini and Bhasmasura — The Boon That Turned on the Hand That Begged for It

panels.title: Kāliya-mardana
panels.label: Kāliya-mardana
panels.summary: The Kāliya-mardana ("the crushing of Kāliya"; also Kāliya-damana, "the subduing of Kāliya," and Kāliya-nartana, "the dance on Kāliya") is the episode in which the boy Kṛṣṇa cleanses a venom-poisoned pool of the river Yamunā by leaping into it, mastering the many-hooded nāga…
panels.alt: The poisoned bend of the Yamunā lies black and still, its trees scorched, one flowering kadamba left alive above it.
panels.artFilmTitle: Kaliya Daman — The Boy Who Danced on the Serpent King

panels.title: Kṛṣṇa-līlā — The Life & Deeds of Krishna
panels.label: Kṛṣṇa-līlā
panels.summary: This file consolidates Krishna's life beyond the Kurukṣetra war (for the war and Gītā, see the Mahābhārata and Gītā deep-dives). The principal source is the Bhāgavata Purāṇa (Canto X = childhood/Vraja/Mathurā; Canto XI = Dwārakā, Uddhava, departure), supplemented by the…
panels.alt: Kṛṣṇa in the groves of Vṛndāvana, a peacock feather in his hair.
panels.artFilmTitle: Kaliya Daman — The Boy Who Danced on the Serpent King

panels.title: Krishna's Infancy Lila
panels.label: Krishna's Infancy Lila
panels.summary: This file is a dedicated deep-dive on the earliest pastoral phase of Krishna's life in Gokula — the demon-slayings of infancy sent by Kaṃsa, the butter-thief (navanīta-cora) cycle, and the two great theophanies of the cradle: Yaśodā seeing the universe in the child's mouth and…
panels.alt: Kṛṣṇa in the groves of Vṛndāvana, a peacock feather in his hair.
panels.artFilmTitle: Kaliya Daman — The Boy Who Danced on the Serpent King

panels.title: Devī Māhātmya / Durgā Saptaśatī — The Goddess's Three Carita
panels.label: Devī Māhātmya
panels.summary: The text is consciously tripartite: each carita ("deed/exploit") is presided over by one of three macro-forms of the Goddess, mapped to the three guṇas. (Wikipedia; traditional Saṃkhya correlation)
panels.alt: Durgā rides her lion toward Mahiṣāsura's army, laughing, and the sound alone shakes the demon ranks.
panels.artFilmTitle: Durga and Mahishasura — The Demon No God Could Kill

panels.title: Sati, the Daksha-Yajna & Parvati — The Goddess Reborn
panels.label: Sati, the Daksha-Yajna &…
panels.summary: This file expands what the master index compresses into a single §4 marriage-cycle line and a §7 pitha footnote. It is the bridge-narrative explaining why the Goddess has two births, how the 51/52/108 Shakti Pithas came to be, and how Shiva was drawn back from grief into…
panels.alt: Dakṣa's great sacrifice burns before an assembly of every god and sage — with no share set aside for Śiva.
panels.artFilmTitle: Sati and Daksha's Yajna — The Origin of the 51 Shakti Peethas
